metadata.name: nfw_open
metadata.description: NFW Open — permissionless creator pools on the NFW mechanism. A fork of nfw with the rewards coupling deleted and a protocol-config fee split.

instructions.name: admit_collection
docs: Admit a collection to the pool. Members of an admitted collection may
be deposited, and a draw ranges over every admitted collection at once.

instructions.name: cancel_group_request
docs: Permissionless: an expired, unmaterialised group request refunds the
purchaser (price less the VRF reserve, plus the escrowed rent) and
advances the group's FIFO.

instructions.name: cancel_request
docs: Permissionless after 15 minutes, and advances the FIFO cursor so one
wedged request cannot freeze the queue.

instructions.name: claim_crown
docs: Permissionless: any active position that beats the incumbent by the
threshold may take the crown, so a dust capture after a vacate cannot
hold against real depth.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone. The crown goes to the position, not to the caller.

accounts.name: reward_vault
docs: Pays the outgoing crown holder when the crown changes hands.

accounts.name: crown_holder
docs: Wallet of the current crown holder, required only when there is an
incumbent with a pot to settle.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone. The money can only ever reach the protocol treasury and
`pool.fee_recipients`, checked by identity and order below, so the
caller earns nothing by calling — which is exactly why no gate is
needed.
This *was* gated on `pool.authority`, directly under a doc comment
claiming it was permissionless (AUDIT-FINDINGS L1). Harmless with one
recipient — the authority claiming its own fees — and false the moment
a second recipient is configured, which is precisely when someone
would rely on it. The gate is gone; the comment is now true.

accounts.name: protocol_config
docs: The one account the creator's `set_fee_recipients` cannot reach. Its
presence here is the enforcement: the sweep will not run without the
config, and the config names the treasury.

instructions.name: clear_collection_bounds
docs: Remove a collection's bounds; the pool-wide pair applies again.

instructions.name: close_group_request
docs: Permissionless housekeeping: reap a materialised or cancelled group
request, rent to the treasury.

instructions.name: close_request
docs: Permissionless housekeeping: reap a settled or cancelled request. The
rent deposit is retained as protocol revenue — disclosed policy.

instructions.name: consume_group_randomness
docs: VRF callback for a group request.

instructions.name: consume_randomness
docs: The VRF callback: the MagicBlock VRF program delivers the oracle's
verified value here, proven by its scoped identity signature. Stores
32 bytes on the request and nothing else — see the module docs.

accounts.name: vrf_program_identity
docs: The VRF program's scoped identity for this callback program —
`PDA(["identity", crate::ID])` under the VRF program id. Its signature
is the proof that the real VRF program, and nobody else, is delivering.

instructions.name: create_group
docs: A group and its escrow. `creator_split_bps` is how much of a pull's
creator share is pooled and split equally across drawable members.

accounts.name: group_creators
docs: The creator allowlist, and the protocol authority who always may.

instructions.name: credit_group_fee
docs: CPI-only: a trusted group program's escrow credits a pool's fee
bucket with a group pull's equal share.

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: Collection membership proof. Anchor pins the program and discriminator;
`require_verified_member` does the semantic layer.
`mut` because Token Metadata's `TransferV1` demands the metadata
writable (it updates pNFT state through it). Only that program can
actually write here; for plain NFTs the flag is inert.

accounts.name: nft_master_edition
docs: Master edition, which prints do not have.
`MasterEditionAccount::try_deserialize` demands `Key::MasterEditionV2`
while a print carries `Key::EditionV1`, so a print cannot be passed here
at all. Without it, anyone holding a master edition with unexhausted
supply could mint unlimited prints — each with `supply == 1`,
`decimals == 0` and an inherited `collection.verified == true` — and
deposit every one for a position.

accounts.name: reward_vault
docs: Pays the outgoing crown holder when the crown changes hands.

accounts.name: crown_holder
docs: Wallet of the current crown holder, required only when this deposit
takes the crown and there is a pot to settle.

accounts.name: admitted_collection
docs: Proof this NFT's collection is admitted to the pool.
Required, not optional: the pool holds many collections, so there is
no implicit one to check against. The seeds pin it to
(pool, that collection), and the handler pins the collection to the
one this NFT's *own verified metadata* names — so admitting collection
A never opens the door to a member of collection B.

accounts.name: allowed_mint
docs: Per-mint allowlist marker, when `pool.allowlist_enabled`. A second,
finer filter *inside* an admitted collection.

accounts.name: depositor_token_record
docs: Token record of `depositor_nft_account`.

accounts.name: vault_token_record
docs: Token record of `nft_vault`; created by the Transfer CPI, depositor pays.

accounts.name: auth_rules
docs: metadata (`require_rules_match`), so the CPI evaluates the real rules
or none — never a substitute account.

accounts.name: collection_bounds
docs: This collection's backing bounds, which may not exist — empty means
the pool-wide pair applies. Deliberately **not** `Option`: an optional
account is one the caller chooses to pass, and a forked client would
simply choose not to. Seeds derive the one address the bounds could
live at, so what the handler reads is the chain's answer, not the
caller's.
Appended last so every account before it keeps its position — a
client built against the previous IDL sends this as a harmless
trailing extra to the old program during rollout.
`effective_bounds` checks emptiness and discriminator.

instructions.name: deposit_core
docs: Deposit a Metaplex Core asset. The sibling of `deposit` for the
account model with no mint — same economics, same events, the §2
plugin gate in place of collection verification.

accounts.name: position
docs: Seeded on the asset address in the seat `nft_mint` occupies for TM
positions — one namespace, no collisions (both are unique account
addresses), and every downstream `position.nft_mint` read keeps
working with "the asset" as its meaning.

accounts.name: asset
docs: The Core asset. `mut` because TransferV1 rewrites its owner field.
asserted by `require_admissible_core_asset` before anything moves.

accounts.name: core_collection
docs: The Core collection account this pool admitted.
account is Core-owned and decodes its plugin set.

accounts.name: admitted_collection
docs: Proof the collection is admitted — the same marker, same seeds, same
rent the TM path uses; the stored pubkey happens to name a Core
collection account instead of a collection mint.

accounts.name: crown_holder
docs: Wallet of the current crown holder, required only when this deposit
takes the crown and there is a pot to settle.

accounts.name: collection_bounds
docs: This collection's backing bounds — identical role, seeds and
non-optionality as on `deposit`: the address is derived, existence is
the chain's answer, and a forked client cannot decline to pass it.
discriminator.

instructions.name: fulfil_group
docs: Permissionless: once the oracle's value is on a group request, pick
the member it selects, create that pool's ordinary request from it,
and credit every drawable member's fee bucket with its equal share.

accounts.name: drawn_pool
docs: The member the caller says the randomness selects. Unchecked because
it may belong to the flagship; the handler checks it is the selected
member and a trusted program's Pool.

accounts.name: drawn_request
docs: drawn program, by CPI); the address is derived and checked.

accounts.name: drawn_reward_vault
docs: the drawn program.

accounts.name: drawn_program
docs: checked against the member's program and `executable`.

accounts.name: drawn_trust
docs: checked against its PDA under the drawn program.

accounts.name: drawn_identity
docs: oracle request the materialised request makes; checked by
derivation under the drawn program (this program's own on the direct
path).

accounts.name: requester
docs: oracle did not take of the reserve, and the rent the address already
held.

instructions.name: fulfill_acquisition
docs: Permissionless — the program re-runs the draw, so the caller has no
influence over the outcome.

instructions.name: grant_issuer_waiver
docs: Trust a Core collection's issuer with the permanent custody powers
its assets carry.
The vaulted-card platforms mint a permanent burn (and freeze)
delegate on every token so they can retire it when the physical ships
— which the plugin gate otherwise refuses, because that same power
reaches an asset sitting in our escrow. This records the authority's
judgment that the issuer is a trusted counterparty for one specific
collection; the deposit UI must say so plainly for waived
collections. See `IssuerWaiver`.

accounts.name: admitted
docs: A waiver may only exist for a collection the pool actually admits —
the same dependency `SetCollectionBounds` enforces, for the same
reason: a waiver for an unadmitted collection is a landmine waiting
for a future admit.

accounts.name: waiver
docs: `init`, not `init_if_needed`: granting twice is a mistake worth
hearing about, unlike bounds, which move with the market.

instructions.name: init_group_creators
docs: Protocol authority: the wallets that may create groups (see
`GroupCreators`); the authority itself always may.

instructions.name: init_group_trust
docs: Protocol authority: which programs' escrows may create requests and
credit fees in this program's pools by CPI (this program is always
allowed). One-time; `set_group_trust` changes it.

accounts.name: protocol_config
docs: The protocol authority is the only one who may say which programs'
escrows may reach into this program's pools.

instructions.name: init_pool
docs: Permissionless. The signer becomes the pool's authority; the protocol
share is enforced at `claim_protocol_fees`, not here.

accounts.name: weight_index
docs: The Fenwick weight index. ~24 KiB, so zero-copy — Anchor's normal
deserialize path would copy it onto the BPF stack.
**Allocated by the client, not by `init`.** Anchor's `init` creates
accounts through a CPI to the system program, and CPI allocation is
capped at 10 KiB (`MAX_PERMITTED_DATA_INCREASE`) — so a PDA of this size
simply cannot be created from inside a program. The client calls
`SystemProgram.createAccount` directly, which has no such limit, and
`zero` here adopts the result after checking it is unused.
The consequence is that the index is a plain keypair account rather than
a PDA, so it cannot be re-derived. `pool.weight_index` records it and
every other instruction checks against that.

accounts.name: sol_vault
docs: Depositor principal. Never holds fees.

accounts.name: reward_vault
docs: Accrued fees: depositor rewards, crown pot, protocol cut. Kept apart
from `sol_vault` so a fee-accounting bug cannot reach principal.

accounts.name: protocol_config
docs: Required on every path since the fee floor landed: the pool's opening
`protocol_fee_bps` is clamped up to `min_protocol_fee_bps`, and this
account is the only first-hand source of the floor — an optional
account here would be a creator-chosen exemption from it. Fixed seeds,
so clients resolve it without being told. Also the floor the
creator-chosen share (`args.protocol_share_bps`) is checked against.

instructions.name: init_protocol_config
docs: One-time, and only by the program's upgrade authority: the signer
becomes the protocol authority and sets the treasury, its share of
every pool's accrued fees, and the fee floor under every pool.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Becomes the protocol authority — and must BE the program's upgrade
authority. Without that pin this initializer is first-caller-wins on a
fixed-seed PDA: on a fresh deploy, whoever landed it before the team
owned the fee authority and the treasury for good. The upgrade
authority is the one key an attacker cannot hold at deploy time, so
the race is closed in code rather than left to runbook discipline.

instructions.name: materialise_group_request
docs: CPI-only: a trusted group program's escrow creates the request a
group pull became, in one of this program's pools.

accounts.name: escrow
docs: The calling program's escrow, signing by CPI. Verified against the
trusted programs' escrow derivation for `group`.

accounts.name: request
docs: checks the address.

accounts.name: pool
docs: checked, and authority-checked (first field, offset 8) in the handler.

instructions.name: migrate_protocol_config
docs: Config authority or the program's upgrade authority. Realloc an
old-layout config up to the current size; the upgrade authority may
also repoint a lost config authority. Idempotent.

accounts.name: protocol_config
docs: checked in the handler; the signer is checked against the stored
authority (offset 8) OR the upgrade authority.

instructions.name: promote_position
docs: Permissionless: a staged position becomes eligible once the draw it was
waiting on has settled.

accounts.name: admitted_collection
docs: Proof the position's collection is *still* admitted.
Without this, `retire_position` would be undone by the next
permissionless `promote_position` — the two would fight, and the
revoked collection would drift back into the draw. Seeds pin it to
(pool, the collection this NFT's own metadata names), so it cannot be
satisfied with some other admitted collection's marker.

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: The position's own NFT metadata, naming the collection above.

accounts.name: head_request
docs: Head-of-queue request, required whenever a draw is open — same shape and
same predicate as `withdraw`, for the same reason (`reveal.rs`).
Promotion moves `active_positions` and, through `index.set`,
`total_weight`. Both are read by `fulfill_acquisition` *after* the
randomness is public: the first through the EV drift guard, the second
as the `uniform_below` bound, which re-rolls the entire descent when it
changes. Ungated, that let anyone read a revealed draw and either force
the request to expire or re-roll it toward inventory they preferred,
composed into a single transaction with the fulfil.

instructions.name: promote_position_core
docs: Promote a staged Core position — `promote_position`'s sibling; the
still-admitted proof reads the asset's own bytes.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone — promotion is housekeeping, exactly as on the TM path.

accounts.name: asset
docs: The position's own asset, read for the collection it names.

accounts.name: admitted_collection
docs: Proof the collection is *still* admitted — without it,
`retire_position_core` would be undone by the next permissionless
promote. Seeds pin it to its own stored collection; the handler pins
that collection to the asset's.

accounts.name: head_request
docs: Head-of-queue request, same shape and predicate as everywhere else.

accounts.name: requester_state
docs: Nonce watermark for this requester, created on their first pull.
The handler requires `args.nonce > requester_state.last_nonce`, which is
what keeps VRF seeds unique now that they derive from the nonce rather
than the global request counter — see `RequesterState`.

accounts.name: oracle_queue
docs: MagicBlock's base-layer oracle queue. Pinned to the one supported
queue: queues are per-oracle PDAs, so a caller-chosen queue would be a
caller-chosen oracle — at best a dead one that wedges the FIFO head
until expiry.

accounts.name: program_identity
docs: Our identity PDA, which co-signs the request CPI. Its signature is how
the VRF program knows the callback target was chosen by this program
and not by a caller naming us.

accounts.name: vrf_program
docs: The one VRF program every pool is allowed to trust. The `Program` type
pins the SDK's id; the constraint keeps `pool.vrf_program` load-bearing
rather than decorative.

accounts.name: slot_hashes
docs: as one input to its request id.

instructions.name: request_group
docs: Pay for one pull over the group, priced as the stock-weighted mean of
its members, and request the oracle's value. The pool is chosen by
that value in `fulfil_group`.

accounts.name: escrow
docs: System-owned, no data: the group's escrow.

instructions.name: rescue_settle_core
docs: Broken-escrow settlement for a DRAWN Core position: `resolve_choice_core`'s
CashOut minus the asset-goes-home leg, same caller/window ladder, same
proof requirement.

accounts.name: asset
docs: The (formerly) escrowed asset — read only for the broken-escrow proof.
`require_escrow_broken`.

accounts.name: protocol_config
docs: The rescue is a CashOut minus the asset leg, so it pays the protocol's
cash-out cut exactly as `resolve_choice_core` does (2026-08-16); a
creator who is also the issuer of a waived collection could otherwise
yank a drawn asset and settle around the floor. Trailing, like the
resolve siblings' pair.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: program-owned refused as at the sweep and the resolves.

instructions.name: rescue_withdraw_core
docs: Broken-escrow exit for a Core position that is NOT mid-draw: the exact
money legs of `withdraw_core`, minus the asset transfer, admitted only
on proof the escrowed asset no longer sits under the position PDA.

accounts.name: head_request
docs: Head-of-queue request, exactly as on `withdraw_core` — the rescue is
still an exit, and the reveal gate applies to exits.

accounts.name: asset
docs: The (formerly) escrowed asset — read only for the broken-escrow proof.
`require_escrow_broken`.

accounts.name: nft_destination
docs: Where the NFT lands. **Who** must own it depends on the branch, so the
check lives in the handler rather than here.
An earlier version pinned `owner == request.requester` in this struct
while `cash_out` separately required `owner == position.depositor`. Both
had to hold at once, so CashOut could only ever succeed when the
purchaser *was* the depositor — the branch was unreachable in practice.
A constraint that is only correct for one branch does not belong on an
account shared by two.

accounts.name: system_program
docs: Needed on KeepAndRelist (purchaser pays in new backing) and on every
pNFT settlement (TransferV1 may create the destination token record).

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: `mut`: `TransferV1` demands the metadata writable.

accounts.name: vault_token_record
docs: Token record of `nft_vault`.

accounts.name: destination_token_record
docs: Token record of `nft_destination`; created by the CPI, caller pays.
as a seeds constraint here; the handler derives and pins it against
the destination it has already validated per-branch
(`require_destination_record`). Token Metadata re-checks in CPI.

accounts.name: auth_rules
docs: metadata (`require_rules_match`).

accounts.name: collection_bounds
docs: The bounds account for this NFT's collection — required by the
KeepAndRelist branch, which sets a fresh backing and must satisfy the
same per-collection rule as `deposit`. Optional in the struct only so
Keep and CashOut keep their transaction shape; the relist handler
refuses to run without it, so a relister cannot opt out. `Option`
rather than seeds because the collection lives in `nft_metadata`,
itself optional — the handler derives the one legal address and pins
this against it (`require_relist_bounds`).
checked by `bounds_if_set`.

accounts.name: protocol_config
docs: Trailing, after the optionals, on purpose (2026-08-16): a client built
against this IDL sends two accounts the previous program simply
ignores as remaining_accounts, so the consoles could ship ahead of the
upgrade instead of racing it. Anchor reads an Option before them by
key, so the order is legal.
The protocol's cut of a cash-out (PROTOCOL_CASHOUT_BPS of the backing)
is paid off the top, straight to the treasury the global config names.
Read here so the payee cannot be substituted; a Keep or relist carries
the two accounts and does not touch them.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: program-owned treasury is refused here as it is at the sweep: pointed
at a sol_vault it would bury the cut in depositor principal (or, at
this pool's own, hit SelfPayout on every cash-out); at a reward_vault
it would be an unbooked donation. Refusing keeps the misconfiguration
loud rather than silent.

instructions.name: resolve_choice_core
docs: Settle a drawn Core position — `resolve_choice`'s sibling: same
three branches, same windows, Core custody moves.

accounts.name: asset
docs: The escrowed asset itself.
the current owner (the position PDA) can move it.

accounts.name: core_collection
docs: The asset's Core collection, along for plugin evaluation.

accounts.name: collection_bounds
docs: Bounds for the asset's collection — required by the KeepAndRelist
branch, which sets a fresh backing. Optional in the struct only so
Keep and CashOut travel light; the relist handler refuses to run
without it (`require_relist_bounds_core`), so a relister cannot opt
out.
asset's own bytes name; emptiness and discriminator checked by
`bounds_if_set`.

accounts.name: protocol_config
docs: Trailing, after the optionals, on purpose (2026-08-16): a client built
against this IDL sends two accounts the previous program simply
ignores as remaining_accounts, so the consoles could ship ahead of the
upgrade instead of racing it. Anchor reads an Option before them by
key, so the order is legal.
The protocol's cut of a cash-out (PROTOCOL_CASHOUT_BPS of the backing)
is paid off the top, straight to the treasury the global config names.
Read here so the payee cannot be substituted; a Keep or relist carries
the two accounts and does not touch them.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: program-owned treasury is refused here as it is at the sweep: pointed
at a sol_vault it would bury the cut in depositor principal (or, at
this pool's own, hit SelfPayout on every cash-out); at a reward_vault
it would be an unbooked donation. Refusing keeps the misconfiguration
loud rather than silent.

instructions.name: retire_position
docs: Move a revoked collection's position out of the draw, leaving it
withdrawable. Permissionless: the marker's absence is a public fact.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone. Retirement is the mechanical consequence of a public fact —
the marker is gone — and it takes nothing from anyone: the position
stops being drawable, its depositor keeps every right they had.

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: The metadata of the position's own NFT, which names the collection it
belongs to. Read first-hand rather than trusted from the caller.

accounts.name: admitted_collection
docs: The admission marker that must **not** exist.
asserted empty in the handler. An account that still exists means the
collection is still admitted and there is nothing to retire.

instructions.name: retire_position_core
docs: Retire a revoked Core collection's position out of the draw —
`retire_position`'s sibling, same rights preserved.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone — the marker's absence is a public fact, and retirement takes
nothing from anyone.

accounts.name: asset
docs: The position's own asset, read first-hand for its collection.

accounts.name: admitted_collection
docs: The admission marker that must **not** exist. The handler derives the
one address it could live at from the asset's collection and asserts
emptiness — seeds cannot read the asset, so the pin moves inward.

instructions.name: revoke_collection
docs: Stop admitting new deposits from a collection. Positions already in the
pool keep every right they had; use `retire_position` to take them out
of the draw as well.

instructions.name: revoke_issuer_waiver
docs: Withdraw an issuer waiver. Future deposits from the collection face
the full plugin policy again; positions already in the pool are
untouched, like every revoke here.

instructions.name: set_collection_bounds
docs: Set (or move) a collection's backing bounds. While the bounds account
exists it replaces the pool-wide min/max for that collection.

accounts.name: admitted
docs: Bounds may only exist for a collection the pool actually admits;
seeds pin this marker to the same collection the bounds name.

accounts.name: bounds
docs: `init_if_needed` because "set" and "adjust as the floor moves" are the
same authority action; splitting them into init/update instructions
would only add a failure mode (calling the wrong one).

instructions.name: set_fee_recipients
docs: Creator-gated, and it governs only the remainder after the protocol
share: the split it sets is applied to what is left once
`claim_protocol_fees` has paid the treasury.

instructions.name: set_group_members
docs: Replace the member list with the pools passed as remaining accounts,
in order; each must be a Pool owned by a trusted program.

instructions.name: set_own_protocol_share
docs: Pool authority: move your own pool between the default share (`None`)
and the listed share (`Some(5000)`), or anything between; below the
global default and above the listed tier are refused. Emits
`PoolProtocolShareChanged` like the protocol authority's setter.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The POOL's authority, this time: the creator moving their own pool
between the two tiers the console offers (2026-08-16). Bounded on both
sides so the instruction can never pay the protocol less than the
global default (the floor `init_pool` already holds a creator to) nor
more than the listed share. Whether the pool is actually listed on
nfw.fun is the directory's decision, off chain: a pool that drops back
to the default share is simply delisted.

instructions.name: set_pool_protocol_share
docs: Protocol authority only: set, move, or clear one pool's override of
the global protocol share. Forward-only at sweep time, no floor (a
below-default retune spends the protocol's own revenue), and every
change emits `PoolProtocolShareChanged`.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The PROTOCOL authority, not the pool's. This is the instruction that
makes the listed tier enforceable: everyone can launch at the default
share, and when a pool is reviewed and indexed onto nfw.fun/packs the
protocol retunes that pool to the listed number. No creator-gated
instruction can reach the field, so there is no promise a creator can
break.

instructions.name: update_protocol_config
docs: Protocol authority only. Forward-only by nature: fees already swept
were split under the config of their day.

instructions.name: withdraw
docs: Never pausable — see the module docs.

accounts.name: head_request
docs: Head-of-queue request, required whenever a draw is open
(`next_fulfillable_id < next_request_id`); pass `None` otherwise. The
handler pins it to the queue head and refuses withdrawal only in the
revealed-but-unsettled window — see the module docs (MH3).
Seeds bind the account to this pool and its own stored identity, so a
withdrawer cannot substitute some other, conveniently idle request;
the handler additionally pins `request_id` to the live cursor.

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: `mut`: `TransferV1` demands the metadata writable.

accounts.name: vault_token_record
docs: Token record of `nft_vault`.

accounts.name: depositor_token_record
docs: Token record of `depositor_nft_account`; created by the CPI, depositor pays.

accounts.name: auth_rules
docs: metadata (`require_rules_match`).

instructions.name: withdraw_core
docs: Withdraw a Core position. Same trust rules as `withdraw`: never
pausable, same reveal window.

accounts.name: head_request
docs: Head-of-queue request, exactly as on `withdraw` — see MH3 there.

accounts.name: asset
docs: The escrowed asset — `position.nft_mint` is its address on this path.
the current owner (the position PDA) can move it.

accounts.name: core_collection
docs: The asset's Core collection, required by TransferV1 for plugin
evaluation.
passing a substitute fails the CPI, never bypasses it.

errors.msg: Arithmetic overflow

errors.name: ParameterOutOfBounds
errors.msg: Parameter exceeds its hard-coded ceiling

errors.name: UnsupportedVrfProgram

errors.name: FeeSplitNotWhole
errors.msg: Fee recipient shares must sum to exactly 100%

errors.name: FeeRecipientMismatch
errors.msg: A fee recipient account is missing or in the wrong order

errors.name: NotAuthority
errors.msg: Caller is not the pool authority

errors.name: NoPendingAuthority

errors.name: NotPendingAuthority
errors.msg: Caller is not the pending authority

errors.name: BackingAboveMaximum

errors.name: TvlCapExceeded

errors.name: NotAnNft
errors.msg: Mint is not an NFT (supply must be 1, decimals 0)

fields.name: batch
docs: How many positions this request drew.

fields.name: backing
docs: Total backing across every position drawn.

fields.name: protocol_cut
docs: Fee split, for the revenue view.

fields.name: nonce
docs: Caller-chosen nonce this account's PDA is seeded on.
The PDA used to be seeded on `pool.next_request_id`, which meant two
purchasers in the same slot built transactions for the *same* address:
one landed, the other failed with "already in use". Safe, but at a
launch moment it makes most pulls fail and reads as the site being
broken. Seeding on `(requester, nonce)` lets concurrent requests queue
instead of collide.

fields.name: request_id
docs: Position in the settlement queue. Still assigned from
`pool.next_request_id` inside the handler, so FIFO ordering is
unchanged — it is simply no longer part of the address.

fields.name: price_paid
docs: Price paid, in full, at request time.

fields.name: vrf_fee
docs: Portion of `price_paid` that covers the VRF and is **not** refunded on
expiry. Without this, an oracle able to withhold an unfavourable draw
turns cancel-and-retry into a free reroll.

fields.name: quoted_ev
docs: EV at quote time. Fulfilment rejects the draw if the pool has drifted
further than this request's own tolerance from it.

fields.name: max_slippage_bps
docs: Purchaser's own drift tolerance, in bps, chosen per request.
A pool-wide setting cannot serve both a buyer who wants certainty of
execution and one who wants price protection. FWA lets the purchaser
pick, up to 100% (accept anything), and so do we — it is their money at
risk, so it is their call.

fields.name: min_pool_backing
docs: Floor on the pool's total active backing at fulfilment.
FWA's `minWeightedValue`. Withdrawals are never blocked, so the good
items can leave between quote and settlement; this lets a purchaser say
"not if the pool has been drained below X".

fields.name: bid_rate_bps
docs: Settlement terms as they stood when this acquisition was paid for.
Settlement used to read these live from `Pool`, which meant
`update_config` could move them while a purchaser sat inside their
decision window — dropping `bid_rate_bps` from 8500 to its 5000 floor
would cut a CashOut from 85% of backing to 50% on a trade already
bought at the old terms. The bounded ceilings capped the magnitude but
not the fact of it.
`quoted_ev` was already snapshotted for exactly this reason on the
pricing side; these are its settlement-side counterparts.

fields.name: protocol_fee_bps
docs: The fee split as it stood when this acquisition was paid for.
Same reasoning as the two above, one step earlier in the money's life:
`distribute_fee` used to read these live from `Pool`, so `update_config`
between request and fulfilment could move a purchaser's *already paid*
fee away from depositors — 0.9 SOL on a 10 SOL batch at the permitted
ceilings. Conservation held either way, which is why the vault's
solvency tripwire could not see it (round six, WP4 F2).

fields.name: request_expiry_seconds
docs: The three windows, as they stood when this acquisition was paid for.
Same reasoning as the four bps rates above, and they were missed for
the same reason — they read like operational settings rather than
terms of a trade. Read live from `Pool` they are both:
* `request_expiry_seconds` — `cancel_request` read it live, and
`validate_config` admits `0`, so the authority could see a **revealed**
draw, set expiry to zero, and cancel the head before it settled. That
is the informed exit the reveal gate exists to prevent (MH3), and it
composed into a single transaction with a `withdraw` of the
about-to-be-drawn position, because cancelling the last queued request
closes `draw_open()` and the gate returns early.
* `resolve_window_seconds` / `final_window_seconds` — read live at
settlement, so dropping the resolve window to zero let the depositor
force `Keep` immediately and void the purchaser's exclusive decision
window, which is part of what they paid for.
Snapshotting rather than flooring, deliberately: a floor would break
the paths that need small windows to be exercised at all — the
suite sets `request_expiry_seconds: 0` and `resolve_window_seconds: 0`
in eleven places precisely so cancellation and forced settlement are
reachable. A snapshot preserves that (the value is fixed before the
request exists) while making a mid-flight change unable to reach a
trade already paid for.

fields.name: randomness
docs: The oracle's verified output, written by `consume_randomness` — the
only instruction that can, and only under the VRF program's scoped
identity signature. All zeroes until `randomness_ready`.
Under ORAO this field was the *address* of a randomness account we
parsed at fulfilment; MagicBlock's callback hands us the 32 bytes
directly (already `sha256`-folded from the proof output by their
program), so the value lives here and fulfilment reads its own state.

fields.name: randomness_ready
docs: Set once by `consume_randomness`. `fulfill_acquisition` refuses to run
without it, and the callback refuses to run twice.

fields.name: randomness_at
docs: When the callback landed. The reveal-window withdraw gate holds only
for `REVEAL_GRACE_SECONDS` past this — bounding the gate by wall clock
rather than by settlement, so an unfulfillable head request cannot
freeze withdrawals until expiry (MH5, AUDIT-ROUND6).

fields.name: seed
docs: Seed committed at request time: `hash(pool || requester || nonce)`.
The seed used to fold in `request_id` instead of `nonce`, which meant
the client had to *predict* the global counter when it created the
randomness account earlier in the same transaction. Two purchasers in
the same slot both predicted the same id; the loser executed against a
shifted counter and failed with `RandomnessMismatch` — the launch-day
collision the nonce-seeded PDA was meant to remove (AUDIT-FINDINGS M1).
Every input is now caller-known at build time, and seed uniqueness is
enforced by `RequesterState`'s strictly-increasing nonce instead of by
the counter's monotonicity.

fields.name: batch
docs: How many positions this request draws.

fields.name: resolved_count
docs: How many of them have been settled. `resolved` flips when it reaches
`batch` — a batch is not done until every drawn position is.

types.name: AdmittedCollection
docs: Per-collection admission marker. Existence *is* the permission.

fields.name: collection
docs: Verified Metaplex collection mint this marker admits.

types.name: AllowedMint
docs: Per-mint deposit marker.
A second filter on top of verified-collection membership, for pools that
want to admit a hand-picked subset. Costs the authority one transaction per
mint, but adds no external program dependency and cannot be spoofed by a
forged `collection` field.

types.name: CollectionBounds
docs: Per-collection backing bounds. Existence *is* the override.
A separate marker rather than fields on `AdmittedCollection` for the same
reason `AdmittedCollection` is not a `Vec` on `Pool` — and for one more:
the admission markers already exist on mainnet at their current size.
Extending that struct would make every un-migrated marker undeserialisable
and brick deposits for its collection until a realloc pass ran. A new
account has no such window: absent means "pool bounds apply", which is
exactly what every collection does today.
When present it **replaces** the pool-wide bounds for its collection, so
the authority can hold a blue chip above `pool.max_backing` without
loosening every other collection. Intersection semantics were considered
and rejected for that reason. `MIN_BACKING_FLOOR` still binds absolutely —
inverse weighting makes dust backing a draw-domination attack, not a
pricing choice (see `weight_of`).
The UI's floor-band confirm remains what it was — advice for honest users.
This account is the part a forked client cannot skip: `deposit` and
`resolve_choice` derive its address from seeds and check on chain whether
it exists.

fields.name: collection
docs: Collection mint these bounds govern.

fields.name: pot_paid
docs: Pot paid out to the outgoing holder.

types.name: CrownVacated
docs: A drawn crown left the head: `fulfill_acquisition` vacates the crown of a
position the draw took, crediting the pot to that position's accrued
rewards rather than paying it out. Emitted so crown trackers see the seat
empty the moment it empties, not at the next handover (review LOW-3a).

fields.name: pot_credited
docs: Pot credited to the drawn position's accrued rewards.

fields.name: staged
docs: `true` when a draw was already open, so the position starts `Staged`.

types.name: EscrowRescued
docs: Broken-escrow settlement: the asset a position escrowed no longer sits
under the position PDA (a waived permanent delegate moved or burned it),
and the position was settled or withdrawn without the asset leg. Paired
with a `Resolved` or `Withdrawn` carrying the money truth.

fields.name: mode
docs: `0` = withdraw-shape (no pending draw), `1` = settle-shape (drawn).

types.name: GroupCreators
docs: Who may create groups. A group pools the drawn pool's creator fee across
its members, so an open `create_group` would let anyone build {their own
pool, a pool they covet} and skim that pool's fee on every pull they route
through the group. The protocol authority names the creators (the open
worker's key for nfw.fun's groups); a creator's own group over their own
packs is an entry here, granted by ops. Its own account, seeded
`group_creators`, so `GroupTrust` keeps the layout the flagship's has.

types.name: GroupFeeCredited
docs: A pool's fee bucket received a group's equal share.

types.name: GroupFulfilled
docs: The oracle's coin chose a pool and the group request became that pool's
ordinary request; from here the pull is the pool's.

fields.name: pool
docs: The drawn pool and the request created in it.

fields.name: price_to_pool
docs: What landed in the drawn pool as that request's price.

fields.name: per_member
docs: The equal share credited to every drawable member's fee bucket.

fields.name: credited
docs: Members that were drawable at fulfilment (and so were credited).

types.name: GroupMember
docs: A pool and the program that owns it.

types.name: GroupRequest
docs: One pull over a group, between payment and materialisation.

fields.name: price_paid
docs: Paid in full at request time into the group escrow.

fields.name: vrf_fee
docs: Withheld on cancellation, as on a pool request.

fields.name: pool_request_rent
docs: Rent for the pool request this will become, escrowed at request
time so materialisation is funded by the purchaser, not the caller.

fields.name: oracle_reserve
docs: Escrowed for the drawn pool's own randomness request at
materialisation (GROUP_ORACLE_RESERVE); what the oracle does not take
goes back to the purchaser in the materialising instruction, and all
of it on cancel.

fields.name: quoted
docs: Each member's EV at quote time, keyed by pool so the set may change
underneath a live request: a member removed since is simply absent
from the live set, a member added since is absent from this list, and
neither is selectable for this request. Zero for a member that was not
drawable at quote time, likewise unselectable. The drift check at
materialisation uses the drawn member's entry.

fields.name: materialised_into
docs: The pool request this became, once it did.

fields.name: materialised_pool
docs: The pool it landed in.

types.name: GroupRequesterState
docs: Nonce watermark per (group, requester), the twin of `RequesterState`.

types.name: GroupTrust
docs: Which programs' escrows may create requests and credit fees in this
program's pools by CPI. Kept in its own account, not on `ProtocolConfig`,
so no live account changes size.

fields.name: pool_key
docs: The pool's identity, and the only seed of its PDA. Any key the creator
picks — deliberately not a collection, because the pool admits many.
One pool is the expected deployment; the argument exists so tests (and
a future migration) can stand up isolated ones.

fields.name: creator_only_deposits
docs: Own-stock mode: only the creator may deposit, and relist is refused
structurally. Init-only; see the fields on `Pool`.

fields.name: relist_enabled
docs: Whether settlement offers `KeepAndRelist`. Init-only, and refused
alongside `creator_only_deposits` by `validate_config`.

fields.name: protocol_share_bps
docs: Optional per-pool protocol share, in bps. `None` (the default) means
the global `ProtocolConfig` share applies and floats with it; `Some(x)`
pins the pool at `x`, requires the `protocol_config` account, and is
floored at the global default — a creator can volunteer MORE (the
listed tier launches at 50% directly) but can never launch below what
the protocol charges everyone, nor above the listed share. Afterwards
the creator moves it inside that same band (`set_own_protocol_share`)
and the protocol authority anywhere (`set_pool_protocol_share`).

types.name: IssuerWaiver
docs: Per-collection waiver of the Core custody-plugin policy. Existence *is*
the waiver.
# What this waives, and what it admits to
`core_plugins.rs` refuses assets whose plugin set lets anyone but the
owner move, burn or freeze them — that is what makes the program's
"nobody but you can touch a deposited asset" promise true on chain. The
vaulted-card platforms (Beezie, Phygitals) mint exactly those plugins:
the issuer burns the token when the physical card ships, so every token
they issue carries a permanent burn (and freeze) delegate by design.
For those assets the promise was never available to make. The issuer
holds the physical; a depositor is trusting them with the card's whole
value before we enter the picture. This marker records the authority's
judgment that a specific collection's issuer is that kind of
counterparty — and every deposit from a waived collection is accepting
issuer risk the UI must state plainly, not bury.
Same account shape as [`CollectionBounds`], for the same reasons: a
separate marker resizes nothing that exists on mainnet, absence means
"the full policy applies", and revocation refunds the rent forward-only
— positions already in the pool are untouched, exactly like
`revoke_collection`.
The waiver narrows, never opens: membership, ownership, decodability and
the external-adapter refusal all still apply. Only the permanent
transfer/burn/freeze refusals are waived.

fields.name: collection
docs: Core collection this waiver covers.

types.name: MaterialiseArgs
docs: Everything a pool needs to create the request a group pull became. The
same struct is the CPI argument to a sibling program's
`materialise_group_request`.

fields.name: nonce
docs: Tagged (high bit set) so it cannot collide with the requester's own
nonces in this pool; see `GROUP_NONCE_TAG`.

fields.name: price_paid
docs: What lands in this pool as the request's price.

fields.name: quoted_ev
docs: The member's EV at group quote time: the drift check already passed
in `fulfil_group`; carried so `fulfill_acquisition` re-checks against
the same figure.

fields.name: protocol_fee_bps
docs: The fee and crown rates this request carries: adjusted by the group
so the pool's own split of `price_paid` still pays the crown and the
depositors what a direct pull of the full price would (see
fulfil_group.rs, "Money, exactly").

fields.name: pauser
docs: Who may call `set_paused`, besides the authority.
Pausing is the only time-critical admin action, and it is the one whose
blast radius is provably bounded: `set_paused` reaches `deposit` and
`request_acquisition` and nothing else, so it cannot trap a depositor's
funds no matter who holds it. Everything else the authority can do is
either slow (parameter tuning) or dangerous (`set_fee_recipients`,
`transfer_authority`).
Fusing the two forced one key to be both fast and trusted, which is the
argument that kept the authority on a single hot key: nobody wants to
collect a second multisig signature during an incident. Splitting the
fast half out means the authority never needs to be fast, and can go
behind a Ledger or a multisig without making an incident worse.
Set to the authority at `init_pool`, so the default behaviour is exactly
what it was before this field existed. Changed with `set_pauser`.

fields.name: pool_key
docs: The pool's own identity, and the only thing its PDA is seeded on.
An arbitrary key chosen at `init_pool`, not a collection: this pool
admits **many** collections, so seeding it on one would have been a
lie as well as a limit. Production runs a single pool — a pull can
land on any NFT in it, across every admitted collection, which is the
product. Multiple pools remain possible (tests use one each), they
simply are not the shape anyone is expected to deploy.
Membership lives in `AdmittedCollection` marker accounts rather than a
`Vec` here: unbounded, one transaction and ~0.0014 SOL each, rent
refunded on revoke, and it keeps `Pool` a fixed size.

fields.name: vrf_program
docs: VRF program this pool trusts for randomness.
Init-only, and `require_supported_vrf_program` admits exactly one value
— `vrf::MAGICBLOCK_VRF_PROGRAM_ID` — in every build. It is stored
rather than assumed so the constraint in `request_acquisition` has
something first-hand to compare against, not so a build can be talked
into trusting something else: the localnet mock runs *at MagicBlock's
own address* via `[[test.genesis]]`, which is what removed the
relaxation flag (AUDIT-FINDINGS #5). This comment previously described
ORAO and a mock-pointing escape hatch; both were gone.

fields.name: vrf_fee
docs: Charged on every request and **not refunded** when a request expires.
See `vrf.rs` for why a refundable expiry would be a free reroll.

fields.name: standard
docs: Asset standard every deposit into this pool must carry. `0` = Token
Metadata (plain SPL and pNFT). Reserved upward for standards with
different account models: `1` = Metaplex Core (docs/core-plan.md §1).
Init-only. One byte of rent bought before mainnet so that supporting
a second standard later is a feature, not a migration.

fields.name: total_backing
docs: Backing of selectable positions. Drives `EV`, so it excludes anything
staged or awaiting resolution.

fields.name: pending_backing
docs: Backing of positions drawn but not yet resolved. Held, not selectable.

fields.name: acc_reward_per_position
docs: Accumulator for the equal split, scaled by `ACC_PRECISION`. A position
is owed `acc_reward_per_position - reward_checkpoint`, which is what
makes "split across all active positions" `O(1)` instead of a loop.

fields.name: pending_fees
docs: Acquisition payments sitting in the reward vault, not yet split.
`request_acquisition` pays the whole price into the reward vault, but
`distribute_fee` does not run until fulfilment — deliberately, because a
price already credited to depositors could not be refunded on expiry.
Between those two points the vault holds real lamports that no other
`Pool` field describes.
Without this, reward-vault solvency is not expressible in pool state at
all: the only way to compute it was to enumerate every live request
through `getProgramAccounts`, which a test can do and a program or a
monitor cannot. With it, `reward_vault_liability()` is an O(1) read.

fields.name: crown_position
docs: Largest-backed position, or `None` when the crown is vacant.

fields.name: crown_depositor
docs: **Wallet** of the crown holder — the account the pot is actually paid to.
Tracked separately from `crown_position` because that is a PDA, and a
Position PDA has no instruction that can move stray lamports back out.
Paying the pot there would strand it permanently.

fields.name: head_since
docs: When `next_fulfillable_id` last moved — i.e. when the current head
request reached the front of the queue.
The reveal gate runs its grace from `max(randomness_at, head_since)`,
because a request can receive its randomness while still queued behind
another and spend the whole window not being settleable. Measuring from
the callback alone let that window lapse before the request was ever
the head, and the gate could then never engage for it — round six, W-1.
See `reveal.rs`.

fields.name: slippage_bps
docs: The pool's **suggested** drift tolerance for purchasers — advisory, not
a ceiling, and deliberately so.
Round six's WP2 flagged this as "a config field that looks like a
guardrail and isn't": `validate_config` bounds it to
`MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS`, which reads like enforcement, while fulfilment
governs on `request.max_slippage_bps` exclusively and nothing consulted
this at all. The complaint was right, and the resolution is to make the
field honest rather than to make it binding.
**Not** turned into an enforced ceiling, considered and rejected:
capping a purchaser's own tolerance contradicts a researched product
decision (`AcquisitionRequest::max_slippage_bps` — FWA lets the buyer
accept any movement, because it is their money at risk), and the
security argument for capping it died with MH4: the draw-capture that
scaled with a purchaser's tolerance required promoting a position into
an already-priced request, which `promote` now refuses. What remains
is a default worth publishing, so it is published and read.
The floor and ceiling that *are* enforced live on the request:
`MIN_SLIPPAGE_BPS` (a zero tolerance is a wedge, not protection — MH5)
and `MAX_BPS`.

fields.name: resolve_window_seconds
docs: Purchaser's exclusive decision window. Configurable rather than
hard-coded so the path can actually be exercised in a test — a deadline
nobody can reach is a deadline nobody has verified.

fields.name: final_window_seconds
docs: After this, anyone may finalise to the default outcome.

fields.name: request_expiry_seconds
docs: After this, an unfulfilled request may be cancelled by anyone.

fields.name: discount_to_depositors
docs: Route the CashOut settlement discount to depositors instead of the
protocol. FWA ships this as a switch; it is the strongest lever there is
for attracting depth, because it is the only thing that pays a depositor
specifically for having been drawn.

fields.name: fee_recipients
docs: Where the creator's share of accrued fees goes, in order, with shares
in bps summing to exactly `MAX_BPS`.
This splits the **remainder**: `claim_protocol_fees` pays the
`ProtocolConfig` treasury its share first, and only what is left runs
through this list. The init default of [authority, 100%] is therefore
honest, and `set_fee_recipients` stays creator-gated because the money
it points is the creator's own.

fields.name: creator_only_deposits
docs: Own-stock mode: only the pool authority may deposit. Init-only. A
creator running their own inventory gets a structural guarantee that
nobody else's assets can enter, without per-mint allowlist rent.
Setting it also forbids relist (see below), because a relist would
seat the winner as depositor and break the mode's one invariant.

fields.name: relist_enabled
docs: Whether `KeepAndRelist` is offered at settlement. Init-only. Relist is
the pool's resupply valve, so a pool with it off shrinks by one item
per Keep and the creator restocks manually. `validate_config` refuses
`true` alongside `creator_only_deposits`, so the stored pair never
claims a combination settlement would refuse anyway.

fields.name: protocol_share_override
docs: Per-pool override of `ProtocolConfig::protocol_share_bps`, read by
`claim_protocol_fees` at sweep time. `None` means the global default
applies, and floats with it; `Some(x)` pins this pool at `x`.
The chain carries a NUMBER, not a tier: "listed" (50%) and
"self-hosted" (25%, the global default) are off-chain policy, so a
future pricing idea is a config write, not a program upgrade.
Two writers, by design:
* the CREATOR, at `init_pool` and via `set_own_protocol_share`
(2026-08-16), held to `[global default, MAX_CREATOR_PROTOCOL_SHARE_BPS]`
so choosing is only ever volunteering more (the listed tier) or
stepping back to the default (a delist by policy), and refused
outright while the field holds a value outside that band;
* the PROTOCOL AUTHORITY, any time, via `set_pool_protocol_share`,
unbounded — a value it puts outside the creator's band is its alone
to move, and every change from either side emits
`PoolProtocolShareChanged` so a creator can watch their own pool.
This does not weaken the argument in `state/protocol.rs` that the
share "cannot live in pool state": that argument is about a creator
paying LESS than the default, and no creator-gated instruction can
take this field below it.

fields.name: authority
docs: Who sets members, the lookup table and the pause. The protocol
authority for nfw.fun's groups; a creator for a group over their own
packs.

fields.name: group_id
docs: Caller-chosen, so one authority may own many groups.

fields.name: members
docs: The set. Order is the order members are passed to `request_group` and
`fulfil_group`.

fields.name: creator_split_bps
docs: How much of a pull's creator share is pooled and split equally across
drawable members; the rest stays with the drawn pool's own recipients.

fields.name: lookup_table
docs: The address lookup table that carries every member's accounts, so a
client can build the v0 transaction without asking. Default = unset.

fields.name: next_request_id
docs: FIFO among this group's requests, the same contract as a pool's.

fields.name: request_expiry_seconds
docs: A group request that has not materialised by then is cancellable for
the standard refund (price less the VRF reserve, plus the pool
request's rent). Fixed at create, the pools' default.

fields.name: head_since
docs: When the current head became the head: on its request if the queue
was empty, else when its predecessor materialised or was cancelled.
The cancel grace is measured from the later of this and the reveal,
as the pools do, so a request revealed while queued is still shielded
for the grace once it is the head.

types.name: PoolProtocolShareChanged
docs: A pool's protocol-share override moved (or cleared): by the protocol
authority (`set_pool_protocol_share`, unbounded) or, since 2026-08-16, by
the creator (`set_own_protocol_share`, inside [default, listed]). Emitted
on every change from either side so a creator can watch their own pool
and the directory can delist one that stepped back to the default.

fields.name: share_bps
docs: The stored override; `None` means the pool reverted to the global
default.

fields.name: effective_bps
docs: What the next sweep will actually charge: the override if present,
otherwise the global default at the time of this change.

fields.name: backing_amount
docs: Committed backing. Sets selection weight *and* funds the standing bid.

fields.name: slot_index
docs: This position's slot in the pool's `WeightIndex`.
The draw returns a slot, and `fulfill_acquisition` requires the passed
`Position` to claim it. That single equality is what replaces the old
design's proof that the caller handed over the complete active set.

fields.name: reward_checkpoint
docs: Snapshot of `pool.acc_reward_per_position` when this position last
settled up. Fees that accrued before it existed are not owed to it.

fields.name: eligible_from_request_id
docs: Staging watermark. A position may only be drawn by requests with
`request_id >= this`, so a deposit landing mid-draw cannot be injected
into a draw the purchaser has already paid for.

fields.name: standard
docs: Asset standard of the escrowed NFT. `0` = Token Metadata (plain SPL
and pNFT alike — those two share every account and differ only in
transfer path, chosen at runtime from the vault's frozen bit).
Reserved upward for standards with *different account models*:
`1` = Metaplex Core (docs/core-plan.md §1). Written once at deposit,
read wherever the escrow's shape — not just its transfer — depends on
what it holds. Added before mainnet precisely so it never has to be
added after.

fields.name: authority
docs: Who may call `update_protocol_config`. Stamped from the signer of the
one-time `init_protocol_config`.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Wallet the protocol's share of every pool's accrued fees is paid to.

fields.name: protocol_share_bps
docs: The protocol's cut of accrued fees, in bps, taken off the top at
`claim_protocol_fees` before the pool's own `fee_recipients` split
runs on the remainder.
Deliberately no policy ceiling below 100% (decided 2026-08-14): the
creator relationship is trust-based and full flexibility is retained.
The only bound is arithmetic, `<= MAX_BPS`, because a share above
100% is not a share. Launch value: 2500 (25%).

fields.name: min_protocol_fee_bps
docs: Floor under every pool's `protocol_fee_bps` (decided with will,
2026-08-15). The protocol's share is a cut of what that rate accrues,
so without a floor a creator could set the rate to zero and starve
the base the share applies to — acute in own-stock pools, where the
creator is also the sole depositor collecting the remainder.
Enforced at `init_pool` (defaults are clamped up to it) and at
`update_config` (args below it are refused). Changeable in BOTH
directions by the protocol authority — it is policy, not a ratchet —
and forward-only for existing pools, which keep their rate until
their creator next writes config.
Trailing field: `migrate_protocol_config` realloc + zero-fill reads
this as 0 on a pre-migration account, which is exactly the old
behaviour (no floor).

types.name: QuotedMember
docs: One member's EV as the purchaser was quoted it.

fields.name: stock
docs: The member's drawable stock at quote time: the selection weight.
Fixed here so nothing that happens to a member between the reveal
and the materialisation (a withdrawal, a deposit, a pause) can
re-roll which member the coin chose; a member that is no longer
drawable when chosen is a refusal, never a re-draw.

types.name: RandomnessDelivered
docs: The VRF callback landed: the oracle's verified value is now stored on the
request and `fulfill_acquisition` can run. Emitted by `consume_randomness`,
which executes inside the *oracle's* transaction — so watching this event
is how off-chain services learn the draw is ready without polling.

fields.name: max_price
docs: Upper bound on what the purchaser will pay, for the whole batch.

fields.name: batch
docs: How many positions to draw.

fields.name: max_slippage_bps
docs: Drift tolerance for this request, in bps. Up to 100% — a purchaser who
wants certainty of execution rather than price protection sets it high.

fields.name: min_pool_backing
docs: Refuse to settle if the pool's active backing has fallen below this.

fields.name: nonce
docs: Caller-chosen, so concurrent purchasers do not target the same address.

fields.name: withheld
docs: Withheld VRF fee. Non-zero is what makes expiry unprofitable to grind.

fields.name: rent_collected
docs: Rent deposit collected as protocol revenue — disclosed policy.

types.name: RequesterState
docs: Per-`(pool, requester)` nonce watermark.
The VRF seed is `hash(pool || requester || nonce)`, and a VRF is
*deterministic*: an oracle asked for the same seed twice returns the same
value — which by then is public. The request PDA alone cannot rule reuse
out once `close_request` exists, because closing a request frees its
`(requester, nonce)` address for re-`init`.
Requiring every nonce to strictly exceed the last one makes seed reuse
unrepresentable in *this* program. MagicBlock happens to mix the request
slot and slothash into its own request id as well, but the guarantee
deliberately does not rest on an upgradeable foreign program's habits.
Clients use a millisecond timestamp as the nonce, which is naturally
increasing and costs the user nothing. The account is created once per
requester per pool, on their first pull.

fields.name: last_nonce
docs: Highest nonce this requester has used in this pool.

fields.name: kept
docs: `true` = purchaser kept the NFT, `false` = took the standing bid.

fields.name: forced
docs: Settled by someone other than the purchaser, after the window lapsed.

fields.name: relisted
docs: `true` = the purchaser kept AND re-armed the position under
themselves; the NFT never left the pool.

fields.name: rewards_paid
docs: Accrued rewards plus any crown pot paid to the departing depositor in
this same settlement — the money the old event shape omitted.

fields.name: protocol_cut
docs: Appended 2026-08-16: the protocol's off-the-top cut of a cash-out
(PROTOCOL_CASHOUT_BPS of the backing), paid sol_vault → treasury in
this settlement. Zero on a keep or relist. `fee` above is what reached
the pool's own fee vault, so the two together are the whole discount.
Trailing so old decoders read the prefix unchanged.

types.name: RewardVault
docs: Holds accrued fees: depositor rewards, the crown pot, and the protocol cut.
Separate from `SolVault` so a bug in fee accounting can never reach
depositor principal. Backing is the thing users trusted us with; fees are
the thing we earned.

types.name: SolVault
docs: Holds every lamport of committed backing for a pool.
Invariant, asserted after every state-changing instruction:
```text
sol_vault.lamports() − rent_exempt_minimum
== pool.total_backing + pool.pending_backing
There is no escrow term. The acquisition payment is a fee and lands in the
reward vault, never here — which is exactly what makes the invariant a
single equality instead of a case analysis over settlement branches.

types.name: WeightIndex
docs: Fixed-capacity weight index for one pool.
Zero-copy because it is ~24 KiB: Anchor's normal deserialize path would
copy the whole thing onto the BPF stack on every instruction that touches
it, which does not fit.

fields.name: pool
docs: The pool this index belongs to.

fields.name: total_weight
docs: Sum of every live weight. Maintained incrementally; equals
`prefix_sum(N - 1)` and is cross-checked against it in tests.

fields.name: high_water
docs: Highest slot never yet allocated. Slots `>= this` are virgin.

fields.name: free_count
docs: Entries currently on the free stack.

fields.name: _padding
docs: Kept for alignment; the index is a keypair account, not a PDA.

fields.name: tree
docs: Fenwick nodes. Not raw weights — `tree[i - 1]` is a range sum.

fields.name: free_stack
docs: LIFO stack of released slots, valid over `[0, free_count)`.
